claims.text: The baseline alloy has the composition W38Ta36Cr15V11 in atomic percent.
The studied W38Ta36Cr15V11 baseline is nanocrystalline.
The baseline W38Ta36Cr15V11 is produced by powder metallurgy using cold rolling, wire drawing, or severe plastic deformation routes.
The baseline alloy exhibits minimal irradiation hardening.
Cr-V-rich second-phase precipitates develop in W38Ta36Cr15V11 during irradiation up to approximately 8 dpa.
The unmodified alloy shows generally good radiation resistance, including an absence of irradiation-induced dislocation loops under the reported exposures.
The Cr-V-rich precipitates in the baseline cause increased hardening.
The unmodified baseline has practical bulk manufacturability.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of 2-3 at.% Hf during powder mixing and consolidation.
Rapid cooling and optimized sintering can keep Hf in solid solution or restrict it to ultrafine clusters rather than large segregated phases.
Dispersed Hf atoms or ultrafine Hf-Cr/V clusters reduce the ability of Cr and V to nucleate larger precipitates.
Hf has a strong affinity for Cr and V and binds them at the atomic level.
Hf-Cr/V binding lowers the local chemical potential for Cr and V segregation and retards precipitate nucleation and growth.
Optimized processing will prevent detrimental Hf-rich secondary phases from forming.

At doses up to approximately 8 dpa and specimen temperatures below 700 degrees Celsius, adding Hf will significantly reduce or completely suppress Cr-V-rich precipitates relative to the unmodified baseline.
The Hf-modified alloy will retain low irradiation hardening, with hardness similar to or only slightly above that of the baseline.
Bulk sintering and manufacturability of the Hf-modified alloy will remain comparable to the unmodified baseline.
Keeping the specimen below 700 degrees Celsius constrains diffusion-driven processes and enables kinetic trapping of solutes.
Above approximately 8 dpa or 700 degrees Celsius, enhanced diffusion may overcome Hf-induced stabilization and permit precipitate formation.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field says the baseline exhibited minimal irradiation hardening, whereas the baseline field says its Cr-V precipitates lead to increased hardening. The prediction then treats hardness similar to the baseline as evidence that low hardening was maintained, leaving the baseline hardening state internally inconsistent.
